items.stem:
Here is a list of numbers.

15   21   23   27   32   36   49   51

From this list, write down

parts.t: the prime number,
the cube number.

sols: A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself.
15 = 3 × 5, 21 = 3 × 7, 27 = 3<sup>3</sup>, 32 = 2<sup>5</sup>, 36 = 6<sup>2</sup>, 49 = 7<sup>2</sup> and 51 = 3 × 17, so all of these have a third factor.
each one splits into a product of smaller factors
23 has no factor other than 1 and 23
A cube number is an integer multiplied by itself three times.
The cube number in the list is 27.
32 is a power of 2 but 32 = 2<sup>5</sup>, which is not a cube

parts.t: Write 108 as a product of its prime factors.
Write down the square number that is a factor of 108 and is greater than 30.

ms:
M1 for a correct factor tree or repeated division reaching 2, 2, 3, 3, 3
A1 (accept 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 3)
sols: Divide by prime numbers, smallest first.
The square numbers among them are 1, 4, 9 and 36.
The only one greater than 30 is 36.

items.stem: 24 = 23 × 3   and   36 = 22 × 32

parts.t: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 24 and 36.
Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 24 and 36.

ms:
M1 for 23 × 32 or for listing 24, 48, 72, … and 36, 72, …
A1
sols: For the HCF take the lower power of each prime that appears in both.
For the LCM take the higher power of every prime that appears.
72 = 3 × 24 = 2 × 36, so it is a multiple of both

items.stem:
At Harbour Bus Station a bus to Marina leaves every 12 minutes and a bus to Riverside leaves every 18 minutes.
A bus to Marina and a bus to Riverside both leave the station at 08 00.

parts.t: Find the next time that a bus to Marina and a bus to Riverside leave the station at the same time.
Work out how many more times before 10 00 the two buses leave the station at the same time.

ms:
M1 for LCM(12, 18) = 36 or for listing 12, 24, 36, … and 18, 36, …
A1 cao
sols: The buses leave together after a number of minutes that is a multiple of both 12 and 18.
LCM(12, 18) = 36, so they next leave together 36 minutes after 08 00.
the lowest common multiple is the first time the two patterns meet
From 08 00 to 10 00 is 120 minutes, and 36, 72 and 108 are the multiples of 36 that are less than 120.

parts.t: Write 300 as a product of its prime factors.
Find the smallest positive integer n such that 540n is a cube number.

ms:
M1 for a correct method reaching 2, 2, 3, 5, 5
A1

M1 for identifying that one more 2 and two more 5s are needed (23 × 33 × 53)
A1 (540 × 50 = 27 000 = 303)
sols: Divide 300 by prime numbers, smallest first.
A number is a cube number exactly when every index in its prime factorisation is a multiple of 3.
The index of 2 must rise from 2 to 3, and the index of 5 from 1 to 3, so one more 2 and two more 5s are needed.
the index of 3 is already 3, a multiple of 3

parts.t: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of P and Q.
Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of P and Q. Give your answer as a product of prime factors.

ms:
M1 for taking the lower power of each common prime (22, 3, 5)
A1

M1 for taking the higher power of every prime
A1 oe (12 600)
sols: For the HCF, use only the primes that appear in both, each to the lower power.
2: lower of 23 and 22 is 22.  3: lower of 32 and 31 is 3.  5: lower of 51 and 52 is 5.  7 appears in Q only, so it is not used.
For the LCM, use every prime that appears, each to the higher power.

items.stem: The Venn diagram shows the prime factors of 84 and of 90.

parts.t: Write down the highest common factor (HCF) of 84 and 90.
Find the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 84 and 90.
Show that HCF × LCM = 84 × 90.

ms:
M1 for 2 × 7 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 oe (all six numbers in the diagram)
A1
sols: The HCF is the product of the numbers in the overlap.
these are the prime factors that 84 and 90 have in common
The LCM is the product of all the numbers in the diagram.
for any two integers, HCF × LCM equals their product

items.stem: For any two positive integers, HCF × LCM = the product of the two integers.

parts.t:
Two numbers have a highest common factor of 8 and a lowest common multiple of 120. One of the numbers is 24.
Find the other number.

Two different numbers have a highest common factor of 6 and a lowest common multiple of 90.
Neither number is 6 and neither number is 90.
Find the two numbers.

ms:
M1 for 6a and 6b with ab = 15 and a, b coprime, or for a correct trial of a pair
A1 both, cao
sols: HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers.
960 = 24 × (the other number), so the other number = 960 ÷ 24 = 40
Both numbers are multiples of 6, so write them as 6a and 6b with a and b having no common factor.
HCF × LCM = product of the numbers
ab = 15 gives a = 1, b = 15 (the numbers 6 and 90, not allowed) or a = 3, b = 5.

items.stem:
A rectangular floor measures 4.5 m by 3.6 m.
It is to be covered completely by identical square tiles, with no gaps and no tiles cut.

parts.t: Find the largest possible length of the side of a tile. Give your answer in centimetres.
Work out the number of tiles needed.

These tiles cost $7.25 each.
Work out the total cost of the tiles.

ms:
M1 for 450 and 360 seen and an HCF method
A1 cao
sols: Work in centimetres: the floor is 450 cm by 360 cm.
A tile of side d cm fits exactly only if d divides both 450 and 360, so the largest tile has side HCF(450, 360).

parts.t: Write 1176 as a product of its prime factors.
Find the smallest positive integer m such that 1176m is a square number.
Find the smallest positive integer k such that 1176k is a cube number.

ms:
M1 for a correct method reaching 2, 2, 2, 3, 7, 7
A1

M1 for identifying that the powers of 2 and of 3 are odd, so 2 × 3 is needed
A1 (1176 × 6 = 7056 = 842)

M1 for needing 32 and 7 to make every index a multiple of 3
A1 (1176 × 63 = 74 088 = 423)
sols: A number is a square number exactly when every index in its prime factorisation is even.
In 2<sup>3</sup> × 3<sup>1</sup> × 7<sup>2</sup> the indices of 2 and of 3 are odd; the index of 7 is already even.
One more 2 and one more 3 are needed, so m = 2 × 3 = 6
A number is a cube number exactly when every index is a multiple of 3.
The index of 2 is 3 ✓; the index of 3 must rise from 1 to 3; the index of 7 must rise from 2 to 3.

items.stem:
Here is a list of numbers.

3   √11   20   22⁄7   π   27   0.65   41

From this list, write down

parts.t: the two irrational numbers,
the cube number,
the two prime numbers.

sols: An irrational number cannot be written as a fraction of two integers; its decimal never terminates or repeats.
<sup>22</sup>⁄<sub>7</sub> is already a fraction and 0.65 = <sup>13</sup>⁄<sub>20</sub>, so both are rational.
11 is not a square number, so √11 = 3.3166… is irrational, and π = 3.14159… is irrational.
20 = 4 × 5 and 27 = 3 × 9 have more than two factors.
3 and 41 have no factors other than 1 and themselves.
41 is not divisible by 2, 3, 5 or 7, and 7<sup>2</sup> = 49 > 41

parts.t: Write down the reciprocal of 1.6.
Find the value of ∛0.027 .

sols: write the decimal as a fraction in its simplest form
The reciprocal turns the fraction upside down: 5⁄8 (= 0.625)
a number multiplied by its reciprocal gives 1

parts.t: Write down all the factors of 45.
Write down all the multiples of 7 that are between 50 and 80.
Explain why 51 is not a prime number.

sols: Look for pairs of numbers that multiply to 45: 1 × 45, 3 × 15, 5 × 9.
stop once the pairs start to repeat
7 × 8 = 56 is the first multiple of 7 above 50, and 7 × 11 = 77 is the last below 80.
The digits of 51 add up to 5 + 1 = 6, which is divisible by 3, so 51 is divisible by 3.
51 = 3 × 17, so 51 has a factor other than 1 and itself and is not prime.

items.stem: The first five triangle numbers are  1,  3,  6,  10,  15.

parts.t: Write down the next two triangle numbers.
Find two square numbers, neither equal to 0, that add up to 100.

√70 lies between two consecutive integers.
Write down these two integers.

sols: The differences between triangle numbers are 2, 3, 4, 5, …
each new triangle number adds the next counting number
15 + 6 = 21 and 21 + 7 = 28, so the next two are 21 and 28

items.stem:
A florist has 36 roses and 60 tulips.
She makes identical bunches, each containing some roses and some tulips, using all the flowers.

parts.t: Find the greatest number of bunches she can make.
For this number of bunches, write down how many roses and how many tulips are in each bunch.

sols: The number of bunches must divide exactly into 36 and into 60, so the greatest number is the HCF of 36 and 60.
lower power of each common prime
Each bunch has 3 roses and 5 tulips
ms:
M1 for listing factors of 36 and 60, or prime factorisation of both
A1

parts.t: Find the total number of factors of N.
Find the smallest positive integer k such that Nk is a multiple of 100.

sols: Every factor of N has the form 2a × 3b × 5c with a = 0, 1, 2 or 3, b = 0, 1 or 2 and c = 0 or 1.
a factor can use each prime up to the power in N
multiply the number of choices for each index
100 = 22 × 52. N already has 23 but only one 5, so one more 5 is needed.
ms:
M1 for (3 + 1)(2 + 1)(1 + 1) oe, or a complete list of factors of 360
A1

items.stem:
Three warning lights on a harbour wall flash at regular intervals.
The red light flashes every 8 seconds, the green light every 12 seconds and the white light every 20 seconds.
All three lights flash together at 21 00.

parts.t: Find the number of seconds until all three lights next flash together.
Work out how many more times all three lights flash together between 21 00 and 21 15.

sols: The lights flash together after a number of seconds that is a multiple of 8, 12 and 20, so find the LCM of the three numbers.
highest power of every prime that appears
They flash together every 120 seconds = every 2 minutes.
So they flash together at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 14 minutes past 21 00: 7 more times.
the flash at 16 minutes is after 21 15
ms:
M1 for a correct method, e.g. listing multiples of 8, 12 and 20 or all three prime factorisations
A1 cao

M1 for 900 ÷ their 120 or for listing 21 02, 21 04, …
A1 FT their (a)

items.stem:
A = 2a × 3b × 7   and   B = 22 × 33 × 5, where a and b are positive integers.
The HCF of A and B is 22 × 32.
The LCM of A and B is 25 × 33 × 5 × 7.

parts.t: Find the value of a and the value of b.
Work out the value of A.

sols: For the prime 2: B has 22. The LCM uses the higher index, and it is 25, so A must have 25.
the LCM takes the higher power of each prime
Check with the HCF: the lower of 2<sup>5</sup> and 2<sup>2</sup> is 2<sup>2</sup> ✓
For the prime 3: B has 33. The HCF uses the lower index, and it is 32, so A must have 32.
the HCF takes the lower power of each prime
Check with the LCM: the higher of 3<sup>2</sup> and 3<sup>3</sup> is 3<sup>3</sup> ✓
ms:
B1 for a = 5
M1 for comparing the index of 3 in the HCF with 33 in B
A1 for b = 2

parts.t:
Two prime numbers have a sum of 45.
Find the two prime numbers. Explain why there is only one possible pair.

Two prime numbers have a product of 221.
Find the two prime numbers.

sols: 45 is odd, so one of the two primes must be even and the other odd.
odd + odd = even, so two odd primes cannot add to 45
The only even prime number is 2, so the other prime is 45 − 2 = 43.
43 is prime: it is not divisible by 2, 3 or 5, and 7<sup>2</sup> > 43
The primes are 2 and 43, and this is the only pair because 2 is the only even prime.
221 is odd, so it has no factor 2; its digit sum is 5, so no factor 3; it does not end in 0 or 5, so no factor 5.
ms:
B1 for 2 and 43
B1 for a reason: 45 is odd so one prime is even, and 2 is the only even prime

M1 for testing primes as divisors of 221, or for 13 or 17 seen
A1 both

items.stem:
A carpenter has three planks of wood with lengths 168 cm, 252 cm and 336 cm.
He cuts all three planks into pieces of the same length, with no wood left over.

parts.t: Find the greatest possible length of each piece.
Work out the total number of pieces he gets when he uses this length.

Instead, he cuts all three planks into pieces of length 28 cm.
Work out how many pieces he gets now.

sols: The length must divide exactly into 168, 252 and 336, so the greatest length is the HCF of the three numbers.
lowest power of each prime common to all three
28 is a factor of 84, so it divides each plank exactly
ms:
M1 for prime factorisations or for a common factor of all three greater than 1 seen
A1 cao

Hence, without using a calculator, find √1764 .

sols: Every index is even, so 1764 is a square number and its square root is found by halving each index.

parts.t: Find the smallest positive integer that leaves a remainder of 1 when it is divided by 4, when it is divided by 6 and when it is divided by 9.
Write down the largest three-digit number that is a common multiple of 4, 6 and 9.

sols: A number that leaves remainder 1 on division by 4, 6 and 9 is one more than a common multiple of 4, 6 and 9.
Common multiples of 4, 6 and 9 are the multiples of 36.
the next multiple, 1008, has four digits

M1 for LCM(4, 6, 9) = 36
M1 for their LCM + 1

items.stem: x and y are positive integers less than 100.

parts.t:
The highest common factor of x and 60 is 12.
Find all the possible values of x.

The lowest common multiple of y and 60 is 180.
Find all the possible values of y.

sols: 60 = 12 × 5. If x is also a multiple of 5 the HCF would be 60, so 60 must be removed.
Every other multiple of 12 has HCF 12 with 60: for example HCF(84, 60) = 12 because 84 = 12 × 7 and 7 has no factor in common with 5.
y must be a factor of 180 = 22 × 32 × 5, and 60 = 22 × 3 × 5 provides only one 3, so y must contain 32 = 9.
The factors of 180 that are multiples of 9 and less than 100 are 9, 18, 36, 45, 90.
ms:
M1 for listing multiples of 12 below 100
M1 for rejecting 60
A1 all seven, no extras

M1 for recognising y is a factor of 180 and a multiple of 9, or for at least three correct values
A1 all five, no extras

parts.t:
A positive integer has exactly three factors.
Explain why the integer must be the square of a prime number, and write down the largest such integer that is less than 200.

M = 2a × 3b, where a and b are positive integers.
M has exactly 12 factors.
Find the smallest possible value of M.

sols: Factors come in pairs d and n ÷ d, so a number has an odd number of factors only when one factor pairs with itself, i.e. the number is a square.
If n = p2 the factors are 1, p and p2; if p were not prime it would bring extra factors. So n is the square of a prime.
Squares of primes: 4, 9, 25, 49, 121, 169, 289, … The largest below 200 is 169
ms:
B1 for a correct explanation (factors 1, p, p2 only)
B1 for 169

M1 for (a + 1)(b + 1) = 12
M1 for at least two of 96, 72, 108, 486 seen
A1 cao

Simplify √48 − √27.
Give your answer in its simplest form.
